title: How EC Has Quietly Changed Form 6 During SIR, Evading Parliament
shows: Traces how the Commission changed Form 6 in each round of the SIR, first adding a declaration in Bihar and later altering the online form itself, with no amendment to the rules. Former Commission officials it quotes say only the government can change the form, under the oversight of Parliament.

title: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 85,854 Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
authors: Sumedha Mittal, Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen
shows: From all 4.3 lakh Form 7 objections the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer published, finds that the roll software generated 85,854 deletion forms giving no reason, carrying the officers' digital signatures. It also counts 1,10,476 deletion requests accepted after the legal deadline.

title: The Mysterious 16.18 Lakh Voters Added to Uttar Pradesh’s Roll
shows: Sets the 71.38 lakh Form 6 applications the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer published against the 84.3 lakh electors added to the final roll. It traces the gap to 16.18 lakh applications taken before the draft, whose names and details were never published as the rules require.

title: Press Note (No. ECI/PN/120/2026): decisions of the meeting of the Commission held on 26.09.2026
shows: The Commission's own record of the nine decisions of its full meeting of 26 September 2026. Among them are home visits by booth level officers in place of hearings for electors sent a notice, a review of ECINET by a committee with an outside expert, and later deadlines for claims in Delhi and Maharashtra. It also says the SIR is complete in 20 states and union territories and orders a drive to enrol those left out.

title: SIR: Deletions go up in Phase 3 with more marked as ‘Shifted’ or ‘Absent’
shows: Finds that the 17 phase 3 states and territories with draft rolls left off 6.15 crore names, 17.1%, against about 12% in the first two phases, with a larger share marked shifted or absent. It also finds that the full deletion lists for Delhi, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana mark no one as 'Others', though the states' press notes report deletions under that reason.

title: SIR: Glaring oddities in Maharashtra’s deletion patterns
shows: Finds that shifted or absent made up 75% to 96.5% of the deletions in 85 Maharashtra constituencies, and that neighbouring seats in Pune used the two reasons very differently. It estimates that the draft roll falls about 1.92 crore short of the projected adult population.

title: In seat Kejriwal lost by thin margin, nearly 40% names added before 2025 polls missing in SIR draft
shows: Follows the New Delhi seat, where the draft removed 37,315 of the 1,08,788 electors on the 2025 roll. It finds that 560 of the 1,430 voters added in January 2025, about four in ten, are missing from the draft.

title: Data analysis: How SIR deletions shaped BJP’s landslide in Bengal
shows: Sets each West Bengal seat's roll shrinkage against the change in the BJP and TMC margin from 2021 to 2026, and finds each point of shrinkage went with a shift of about 0.38 points toward the BJP. The same test on Bihar finds no such pattern, and the authors describe the Bengal result as an association.

title: Power Without Oversight: India’s SIR Judgment and the Unfinished Business of Institutional Design
shows: Reads the Supreme Court's SIR judgment against the scholarship on independent electoral bodies and argues that the Commission holds wide power over the rolls without matching accountability.

title: Bihar SIR Judgement: Three doctrinal gaps
shows: Argues that the judgment of 27 May 2026 relies on one half of the 2024 Section 6A ruling, accepts the Commission's reasons for a special revision without a record behind them, and narrows the 1995 Lal Babu Hussein judgment on deletions.

title: Two ECs dissent, questions on legality of SIR process: Constitutional, legal issues & nuances
shows: Shekhar Gupta goes through the Indian Express report of the two Election Commissioners' 14 objections, what it shows and what it does not, and the constitutional and legal questions it raises.
